display.title: Episode 435: The Rambam's Grave (Shiva Asar B'Tammuz)
display.summary_short: A quiet show for Shiva Asar B'Tammuz: why the Three Weeks are sad and how to end them, the life of the Rambam, and the miracle that showed where he was to be buried.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Shiva Asar B'Tammuz 5750, the first day of the Three Weeks, and so without the usual drums and march. Uncle Yossi explains how the siege of Yerushalayim that began on Asarah B'Teves led to the breaching of its walls on 17 Tammuz and the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash on Tisha B'Av. We ask Hashem 'until when?', but Hashem also waits for us to be ready for Moshiach through more Torah and mitzvos. He passes on the Rebbe's call for everyone to learn Rambam daily. Story time tells the life of the Rambam, born in Cordova, driven from place to place, saved from a storm at sea, who finally settled in Egypt and wrote his great works. Before his passing he asked to be buried in Eretz Yisroel without saying where, and as the cities argue, robbers ambush the funeral caravan in the desert. At this suspenseful moment two young brothers recite the Shema in Studio 604. The story resumes: robbers who try to touch the coffin fall lifeless, and the camel walks on by itself to Teveria, where it kneels at the Rambam's resting place. The show ends with a prayer for a sick child and tzedakah.
display.lesson: Hashem guards the Jewish people and the honor of tzaddikim; we can turn the sad days into days of joy by learning more Torah and doing more mitzvos.
